Software · Essay 003

Small software is a big idea

The next important app may be a sharp, strange instrument made for twelve thousand people.

By The EditorsOctober 3, 2026 · 5 minute read
Filed under
Software / Craft

Software learned the logic of the factory: acquire everyone, standardize everything, and make each additional user cost almost nothing. Scale became more than a business model. It became an aesthetic.

But tools built for everyone tend to understand no one particularly well. Their edges are sanded down by the imagined median user.

Precision beats breadth

There is another tradition: the focused instrument. Software with a point of view, built for a community legible enough to name. These products can encode deeper workflows because they do not need to pretend every workflow is the same.

Small is not a failure to become large. It is permission to become specific.

AI lowers the cost of making and maintaining this class of product. Tiny teams can support features that once demanded departments. Bespoke can become repeatable without becoming generic.

A healthier ecology

The web needs more gardens and fewer shopping malls. More tools that can be understood, repaired, and cared for by the people who make them.

The opportunity is not to build less ambitious software. It is to aim ambition at depth.
